name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
rawDescription: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
highLevelGoals: To efficiently submit product proposals to La Reine Marlene for evaluation.
To receive timely and clear feedback on submitted product proposals.
To effectively evaluate and manage supplier product proposals for approval or rejection.
To maintain and update system configurations to ensure smooth business operations.
To accurately verify and process incoming goods upon their arrival at the stores.
To continuously monitor inventory levels and ensure stock accuracy.
To ensure that inventory replenishment is automatically triggered when stock levels are low.
To easily browse and purchase desired products through the online platform.
To securely complete payments for online purchases using various available methods.
To accurately track the status and progress of their purchased product deliveries.
To efficiently manage and resolve customer support requests and tickets.
To ensure that customer support requests are responded to within defined deadlines.
To effectively reassign support tickets when necessary to ensure timely resolution.
To gain comprehensive insights into overall business performance through data analysis.
To monitor key operational metrics related to orders, sales, inventory, and customer support.
lowLevelGoals: Supplier initiates the creation of a new product proposal within the system.
Supplier inputs specific product information such as name, description, category, and proposed price into the proposal form.
Supplier uploads relevant images for the proposed product to be included with the proposal.
Supplier attaches any necessary supporting documents, such as certifications or specifications, to the product proposal.
Supplier formally submits the completed product proposal to the system for administrator evaluation.
Supplier checks the current status of a submitted product proposal (e.g., pending, approved, rejected).
Supplier accesses and reads specific feedback comments provided by the administrator on a submitted proposal.
System sends an automated notification to the supplier when the status of their product proposal changes.
Administrator views a list of all product proposals awaiting their review and action.
Administrator opens a specific product proposal to examine all submitted details, images, and documents.
Administrator marks a product proposal as approved, indicating it meets company standards.
Administrator marks a product proposal as rejected, indicating it does not meet company standards.
Administrator provides specific textual feedback or reasons for the approval or rejection of a proposal.
Administrator adds, modifies, or deletes product categories available in the system.
Administrator sets up or adjusts rules and algorithms for product pricing, discounts, or promotions.
Administrator assigns or revokes specific roles and access permissions for different user types within the system.
Administrator configures system-wide notification settings, including triggers and recipients for various events.
Warehouse staff uses a scanner to read the barcode of an incoming product for identification.
Warehouse staff inputs the exact quantity of a specific product received into the system.
Warehouse staff assigns or confirms the physical storage location for newly received goods.
System automatically creates a formal document confirming the receipt of goods after verification.
Warehouse staff checks the real-time quantity of a specific product currently in stock.
Warehouse staff searches for product information using its Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) or name.
System provides a detailed report on current inventory status, including quantities and locations.
Warehouse staff manually corrects discrepancies in the recorded stock count for a product.
Warehouse staff or Administrator defines the minimum stock levels for products that will trigger automatic replenishment.
System sends an automated notification to warehouse staff when a product's stock falls below its defined replenishment threshold.
System automatically creates a purchase order for a product when its stock level meets the replenishment criteria.
Warehouse staff reviews purchase orders that have been automatically created by the system for replenishment.
Customer navigates through the available product categories and listings on the online platform.
Customer uses a search bar to find specific products by entering keywords or phrases.
Customer clicks on a product to see its detailed description, specifications, images, and price.
Customer places a selected product into their virtual shopping cart.
Customer modifies the number of units for a specific product within their shopping cart.
Customer deletes a product from their shopping cart.
Customer initiates the checkout process from their shopping cart to finalize the purchase.
Customer chooses their preferred payment method (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) during checkout.
Customer inputs necessary payment details, such as credit card number or login credentials for a payment gateway.
Customer authorizes the payment to complete the purchase.
System sends an automated notification to the customer confirming successful payment.
Customer accesses a list of all their past and current online orders.
Customer obtains the tracking number and carrier details for a specific order.
Customer views the current shipping status of their order (e.g., 'shipped', 'in transit', 'delivered').
System sends automated notifications to the customer regarding changes in their order's delivery status.
Customer Support Agent accesses a list of all unresolved customer support requests.
Customer Support Agent takes ownership of an unassigned support ticket.
Customer Support Agent records private notes or updates related to a ticket for internal team reference.
Customer Support Agent composes and sends a reply to the customer regarding their support request.
Customer Support Agent changes the status of a support ticket (e.g., 'in progress', 'awaiting customer', 'resolved').
Customer Support Agent marks a support ticket as resolved and closed.
Customer Support Agent sorts and filters support tickets based on their priority level or approaching deadline.
System sends an automated alert to the Customer Support Agent when a ticket's response deadline is approaching.
System automatically records the time taken by an agent to provide the first response to a customer support ticket.
Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to a different individual agent for resolution.
Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to a specialized department or team.
Customer Support Agent checks the current number of active tickets assigned to other agents or departments.
Company Manager requests and views a report detailing sales figures, trends, and revenue over a specified period.
Company Manager accesses data and statistics related to new customer sign-ups and acquisition channels.
Company Manager views a dashboard summarizing key financial performance indicators and profitability metrics.
Company Manager downloads raw or aggregated business data in a compatible format for use with external analytical tools.
Company Manager monitors the number of orders placed within a recent time frame in real-time.
Company Manager views the rate at which inventory is sold and replaced over a period.
Company Manager views the percentage of customer support tickets successfully resolved within a given period.
Company Manager views graphical representations of sales data over various timeframes to identify trends.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are accurate and cover the main roles described in the system (Suppliers, Administration, Warehouse/Inventory, Customers, Support, and Management). However, the description explicitly mentions "physical and online purchases." While "Customer" covers the online aspect, the physical purchase process typically involves a "Store Clerk" or "Sales Associate" who assists customers in-store and processes payments, distinct from the online self-service flow. Omitting this role is a minor gap given the explicit mention of physical purchases.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are comprehensive and accurately reflect the functional requirements described in the software description. They cover all major actors (Supplier, Administrator, Warehouse Staff, Customer, Customer Support Agent, Company Manager) and their respective responsibilities (proposals, evaluation, inventory, purchasing, support, analytics). The goals are functional in nature, focusing on the 'what' and 'why' of the system's capabilities without delving into technical implementation details. There are no contradictions with the description, and no significant functional areas appear to be omitted. The truncation in the text (e.g., "l…", "supp…") is likely a formatting artifact and does not affect the semantic correctness of the goals.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive, well-structured, and accurately reflect the functional requirements derived from the high-level goals and software description. They correctly map to the defined actors and cover all major processes (proposals, inventory, e-commerce, support, analytics). There are no contradictions, out-of-context items, or significant omissions. The goals are appropriately granular for a low-level specification.
